decision: How should the parent's assessment report be structured: what leads, and how are the level, the 4 strands, speed and accuracy, the child's work, how we help and the call to action grouped?
route: /report-prototype?variant=A-E&child=behind|on|ahead&stage=1|2|3&prov=BC|ON&help=0|1&view=page|email (dev and preview deploys only; 404 in production)
invariants: same sample data and copy in every variant (src/components/report-prototype/data.ts); every number is sample data except the two FSA figures from the spec

same shared parts: K-8 scale, FSA line (grades 4 and 7), comparison by stage, strand status chips with question counts, speed beside accuracy, work images with high-confidence comments only, how we help by verdict, card (BC) or waitlist (other provinces), help warning
warm look tokens: Geist, Geist Mono labels, soft grey cards, grainy colour fields, 6 px controls
laptop 1440 and tablet 768; phones are out of scope for the test, so the report is not tuned below 700 px

states.child: behind = Maya, grade 4 working at grade 3; on = Leo, grade 4 at grade 4; ahead = Noor, grade 3 at grade 5 (no FSA line: shows the grades-4-and-7 rule)
states.stage: 1 = scale + FSA line (n < 100); 2 = bands among Unica children (n 214, sample); 3 = percentile (n 512, sample)
states.prov: BC = plan buttons, card saved, charge when the first book ships; ON = waitlist
states.help: help flag on shows the 'level may be too high' warning
states.view: email = the report email, 600 px single column, carrying the variant's lead

options.name: Report card
options.bet: A printable school-style document: header table, level sentence, scale, a strand table, facts, work, next steps
options.benefit: Familiar to parents; reads as serious and honest; maps 1:1 to the email and a PDF
options.cost: Least visual; the scale is the only picture
options.risk: Feels like a school report card, which can sting for a child who is behind

options.name: The ruler
options.bet: One huge K-8 ruler in a colour field answers 'behind, on or ahead?' at a glance; each strand is a meter with three zones
options.benefit: Visuals over words (Savar, D-084); the answer is clear in under 5 seconds
options.cost: The hero takes a full screen before any detail
options.risk: Meters imply more precision than 8-10 questions per strand can carry

options.name: Dashboard
options.bet: Every part is a tile, all visible at once, like an account page
options.benefit: Fastest scan; fits the account area and later retakes side by side
options.cost: No reading order; every tile has the same weight
options.risk: Reads as an app dashboard, not a letter about a child; weak for the child reading along

options.name: Read it together
options.bet: One idea per screen in plain words, strands grouped by status ('sure of', 'getting there', 'work on next'), for a parent and child reading side by side
options.benefit: Kindest for a child who is behind; best for story 22 (child sees the report with the parent)
options.cost: Longest page (about 4 screens at 1440); the plan button is at the very end
options.risk: A parent who wants the numbers must scroll for them

options.name: Show the work
options.bet: A short headline with the scale, then each strand beside the child's own work for that strand
options.benefit: Trust: every status sits next to real evidence (stories 37 and 57)
options.cost: Strands with no shown-work question look empty
options.risk: Depends on good whiteboard images; weak or blank work makes the page look thin

open_questions: Show the BC FSA line to families outside BC? The spec ties it to grades 4 and 7 only; the prototype shows it for every province.
Which variant's lead should the email carry? The email view shows each lead; the real email is rebuilt in table markup for the chosen direction.
evidence: Screens per variant: <id>-behind-bc-stage1-1440, <id>-on-ontario-stage2-768, <id>-ahead-stage3-help-1440, <id>-email-behind-bc. No horizontal overflow at 1440 or 768 in any of the 20 captures.
